ip_top_stories.title: Suno narrows AI music claims in US, but most plaintiff copyright claims survive
ip_top_stories.summary: A US court has allowed most copyright claims against AI music generator Suno to proceed, while Suno succeeded in narrowing some of the claims against it. The ruling is a significant development in ongoing litigation between record labels and AI music companies over training data use.

ip_top_stories.title: Round Hill Sues Over AI Training: Copyright Claims Could Reach $1 Billion
ip_top_stories.summary: Music rights company Round Hill has filed a copyright lawsuit over the use of its catalogue for AI training, with potential damages estimated at up to $1 billion. The case adds to growing litigation from rights holders targeting AI developers over unlicensed use of copyrighted works.

ip_top_stories.title: ByteDance and Motion Picture Association signs AI copyright agreement
ip_top_stories.summary: ByteDance has signed a copyright agreement with the Motion Picture Association covering AI, marking a notable voluntary licensing arrangement between a major AI company and a leading entertainment industry body. The deal could signal a broader shift toward negotiated licensing frameworks in the AI sector.

ip_top_stories.title: Naver's pre-ChatGPT AI disclosures disputed in South Korean copyright trial
ip_top_stories.summary: A South Korean copyright trial involving Naver has seen disputes over the company's pre-ChatGPT AI disclosures, with the case centring on what the company revealed about its AI training practices before the generative AI boom. The trial is closely watched as South Korea develops its approach to AI and copyright.

ip_top_stories.title: South Korea Opens the Door to Copyright Registration of AI-Assisted Works
ip_top_stories.summary: South Korea has moved to permit copyright registration of works that are AI-assisted, provided there is sufficient human creative contribution. The policy shift positions South Korea among jurisdictions actively developing frameworks to address AI-generated content under copyright law.

ip_further_links.title: Record Labels Can Pursue Piracy Claim Against AI Song Generator
ip_further_links.summary: A court has ruled that record labels may proceed with piracy claims against an AI song generator, further expanding the legal front for music copyright holders against AI companies.

ip_further_links.title: Snapchat Firm Fails to Duck YouTube-Scraping, AI-Training Claims
ip_further_links.summary: A court has declined to dismiss claims against a Snapchat-linked firm accused of scraping YouTube content for AI training, allowing copyright and related claims to proceed.

ip_further_links.title: Japan urges AI firms to disclose training data to combat IP infringement
ip_further_links.summary: Japan's government is pushing AI companies to disclose what data was used to train their models, as part of efforts to address intellectual property infringement concerns.

ip_further_links.title: German court says AI comic based on dog photo did not violate copyright
ip_further_links.summary: A German court has ruled that an AI-generated comic based on a photograph of a dog did not infringe copyright, providing an early judicial data point on AI-generated derivative works in Europe.

ip_further_links.title: Who Owns the Copyright in Work Generated by an LLM?
ip_further_links.summary: A legal analysis examines the question of copyright ownership in works produced by large language models, surveying current doctrine and the gaps it leaves unaddressed.

ip_further_links.title: The Heart of AI is Not the Code; It is the Weights: Why Model Weights sit outside conventional Intellectual Property doctrine
ip_further_links.summary: An analysis argues that AI model weights — not source code — are the true locus of value in AI systems, and that existing IP doctrine is poorly equipped to protect or regulate them.

ip_further_links.title: Book Publishing Is Being Flooded by AI – and Nobody Knows What to Do
ip_further_links.summary: A report examines the surge of AI-generated books entering the publishing market and the industry's lack of consensus on how to respond.

ip_further_links.title: Random House Suspends Fall Title Due to Plagiarism Concerns [Metered]
ip_further_links.summary: Random House has suspended publication of a forthcoming title following plagiarism concerns, in a case that raises questions about editorial oversight in the era of AI-assisted writing.

ip_further_links.title: 'Getting away with murder': MPs agree big tech is breaching copyright by using NZ content, split on how to respond
ip_further_links.summary: New Zealand MPs have reached broad agreement that big tech companies are breaching copyright by using local content to train AI models, but remain divided on the appropriate legislative or regulatory response.

ip_further_links.title: The Grueling Fight Over Who Profits From AI Music [Metered]
ip_further_links.summary: A detailed look at the complex and intensifying battle between AI music companies, rights holders, and artists over revenue and copyright in AI-generated music.
